messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: network.degradation detected for customer Bluefin over DX-123 / MPLS-peering (severity: high). Visible symptoms: partial packet loss, ~30% latency spikes. Impacting API endpoints behind private VPC peering. Paging Network Oncall.
Network Oncall: ack. Investigating. Can someone pull BGP neighborship and route counts from edge-rt1?
Sarah H: on it, logging into edge-rt1 now.
Sarah H: quick outputs:
```
show ip bgp summary | include DX-123
Neighbor 10.20.30.1     4    180    0    00:02:15    12345    established
Neighbor 10.20.31.1     4    120    0    00:00:12    54321    established
```
Sarah H: both neighbors established but seeing anomalous route churn for Bluefin prefixes (route count oscillating).
Kyle P: any signs of AS path loops or REFLECTOR behavior?
Maria G: pulling route table for 10.7.0.0/16 (Bluefin CIDR)
Sarah H: here's the BGP path for one affected prefix:
```
show ip bgp 10.7.12.0/24
Paths: (4 available, best #2, table default)
  65001 65100 65001 i
  65001 65002 65001 i
  65001 65100 65001 i
  65001 65002 65001 i
```
Sarah H: that looks like the same AS prepended twice — suspicious. Could be reflection between the MPLS PE and Direct Connect.
RoutingBot: automated hint: repeated AS in AS_PATH typically indicates route reflection loop or misconfigured AS path prepend on provider edge.
Network Oncall: I'm seeing intermittent next-hop flips too, which explains partial blackholing. Reached out to Telco. @Telco Support pinged.
Telco Support: confirmed we are seeing routes for Bluefin being reflected between PE-A and PE-B in our fabric. Working the circuit team. ETA 20m for initial mitigation.
Kyle P: need immediate workaround to stop loops — propose applying outbound route-map to strip AS_PATH prepend from our DX advertisement to the MPLS peer, and tag with community so provider doesn't reflect back. Can anyone push on edge-rt1?
Maria G: I can apply an inbound distribute-list to drop routes that show our ASN twice as a stop-gap. Suggest: `route-map DROP_LOOP permit 10 \n match as-path 1 \n set metric 100` then apply `neighbor x.x.x.x route-map DROP_LOOP in`. AS-PATH ACL 1: `^65001 65001$` (example).
Sarah H: pasted exact commands in staging, looks good. Ready to apply to edge-rt1-eu.
Network Oncall: apply to edge-rt1-eu now, I'll monitor.
Sarah H: applied to neighbor 10.20.30.1 (MPLS PE).
Network Oncall: confirmed route table shows removal of the reflected path within 2 mins for the affected prefixes. Ping to Bluefin API now shows recovery on most POPs.
Kyle P: good. Keep this as temporary until telco confirms fix. We should not keep dropping without provider coordination.
Telco Support: we are deploying a fix to stop route reflection at the provider edge (config change to route-reflector policies). Rolling across both PEs; should converge in ~15m.
Maria G: re-running traceroute from our edge to Bluefin backend prior to fix:
```
traceroute 10.7.12.5
 1 10.0.0.1 1.2 ms
 2 100.64.1.1 35 ms
 3 192.0.2.45 120 ms
 4 203.0.113.5 * * *
```
Maria G: after temporary route-map applied, traceroute shows next-hop stabilized through 100.64.1.1, no more * hops. Latency reduced.
Network Oncall: marking customer impact: partial (some POPs affected), duration so far ~18m, mitigation applied (route-map + provider fix in progress).
Incident Bot: :memo: Incident created: INCIDENT-2003456789. Initial severity: P2 -> holding for Telco fix confirmation.
Kyle P: action items — (1) keep route-map for now, (2) coordinate with Telco for rollback steps, (3) run full prefix reconciliation once provider confirms. I'll take lead on postmortem.
Sarah H: I'll join for postmortem, collect BGP logs and route churn graphs.
Telco Support: provider fix rolled on PE-A and PE-B. We've stopped reflecting our ASN. Please confirm on your side.
Network Oncall: confirming - route churn subsided, prefix counts stable for 18 minutes. Latency normalized.
Maria G: running health checks against Bluefin's critical endpoints — all green.
Network Oncall: downgrading to monitoring. Will keep incident open until 00:00 UTC for stability window.
Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: update saved to INCIDENT-2003456789. Assigned: Kyle P (postmortem), Sarah H (data collection).
Kyle P: quick note for postmortem — vendor config change caused unintended reflection due to route-reflector policy mismatch with customer MPLS tagging. Also look at our pre-peering validation to catch AS duplication.
Sarah H: uploading bgp dump and route-change timestamps to the incident folder.
Network Oncall: handing off to next shift @Maria G - please monitor and escalate if we see reoccurrence.
Maria G: ack handoff. Monitoring now.
Incident Bot: :bell: Handoff complete. Next-check at 2003457389.
